# Recreation Prompt

Recreate a mobile-first browser branching narrative game titled `Button Door: The Other House`. Preserve the mechanic truth of a five-turn choice loop: the player taps Start, reads a prompt, chooses one of three options per turn, accumulates one of three visible score tracks, and receives a score-tier ending after the fifth choice with a restart button. Reinterpret the game as Coraline-inspired button-eyed dark fantasy: a brave child in a yellow coat faces an alternate domestic world, the Other Mother, stitched doors, buttons, thread, mirrors, and uncanny temptations. Use procedural browser-native CSS/canvas visuals: black button eyes with cross-stitches, thread fog, wallpaper grain, glowing little door, storybook cards, and mobile-safe bottom dialogue controls. Use catalog-approved Creepster, Cinzel, and Rajdhani fonts plus failure-tolerant eerie/mysterious/dark audio cues gated behind user taps.
blueprint_markdown:
# Blueprint

## Current implemented game identity
- genre: mobile-first branching narrative choice game with animated canvas backdrop and score-based endings.
- objective: make one choice on each of five story turns, accumulate one of three affinity scores, and reach one of ten text endings.
- input model: tap/click start, tap/click one of three choice buttons each turn, tap/click restart after ending.
- core loop: show dialogue prompt, present three choices, apply a numeric score delta to one track, update HUD, advance to the next prompt, resolve ending after five prompts.
- fail/friction state: no arcade failure mid-loop; low or poorly distributed score resolves to a failure ending, while dominant tracks resolve to tiered endings.

## Protected mechanics
- Five sequential prompt turns with exactly three selectable choices per turn.
- Three tracked score dimensions, zeroed on start/restart and displayed in HUD.
- Choice click applies the configured score delta, advances exactly one turn, and may show short feedback.
- Ending selection uses the dominant score track, with a low-score fallback failure state and tiered outcomes.
- Start and restart are native tap/click controls; no global touch suppression is used.
- Animated canvas background and responsive portrait HUD remain non-blocking presentation layers.

## Remixed target
`Button Door: The Other House` reframes the protected branching-choice loop as a Coraline-inspired dark-fantasy storybook nightmare. The player is a brave child navigating the alternate domestic world, choosing between Bravery, Temptation, and Stitchcraft. The authored scene uses procedural button eyes, thread lines, a little door, a yellow-coated child silhouette, and mobile-readable bottom dialogue controls while preserving the original scoring, progression, and ending semantics.
